target.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a restricted agent could create a recurring cron job with a trigger script and a `systemEvent` payload, then have that script receive the full coding tool surface. Main-session cron jobs require `systemEvent`, so the common path bypassed the creator's tool policy whenever cron triggers were enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator tool cap now applies whenever a cron job has a trigger script, in addition to isolated `agentTurn` jobs. The cap is retained on every cron payload shape, survives updates, is persisted through the cron SQLite store so it survives a gateway restart, and is passed to the headless trigger evaluator. This keeps the existing agent-turn behavior while covering main-session system events and command payloads.

Distinct from #12736, which concerns global cron deny policy; #97317 and #101349, which concern isolated agent-turn defaults; and #41484, which concerns elevated execution scope.

## User Impact

Agents restricted to a small tool set can use cron triggers without acquiring shell, exec, or patch capabilities beyond that set. Existing unrestricted operator-created cron jobs continue to work with their configured policy.

## Rebase onto current main

This branch was rebased onto current `main`. Three things needed re-expressing against main's current code, none of which change the fix:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` conflicted because `main` replaced `Type.Object({...}, { additionalProperties: false })` with the `closedObject()` helper. The cap fields were re-expressed in that helper form.
- The changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet that landed on `main` in #106387 forbids an already-oversized file from growing. `src/cron/service/jobs.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` are all over the limit, so the cap additions tripped the gate. Cohesive declarations were hoisted into three companion leaf modules, mirroring the existing sibling convention: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.types.ts` (type-only), `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.types.ts` (type-only wire types), and `src/cron/service/payload-merge.ts` (the cron payload merge rules the patch touches). All three source files are now back at or below their baseline line counts and the ratchet passes.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` now uses the repo's `expectDefined` helper for indexed job access, which main's tightened unchecked index access requires.

## Evidence

- The touched suites were re-run after the rebase with `node scripts/test-projects.mjs` and all pass: 145 checks in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`, 199 checks across `src/cron/normalize.test.ts`, `src/cron/store.test.ts`, `src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts` and `src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts`, and 23 checks in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/cron-validators.test.ts`. 367 checks total.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` restart-aware round-trip coverage for the `systemEvent` and `command` tool caps; both fail on the pre-persistence codec and pass here.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` both pass, `node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` passes, and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files is clean.
- An earlier restart cap-loss and reload proof, pinned to a previous head, is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104430#issuecomment-4945702410

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A cron trigger script created by a restricted caller must not receive tools the caller cannot use; a `systemEvent` main-session job with a trigger script previously kept no tool cap.
Real environment tested: The production `createCronTool` entry point (`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`) driven via `tool.execute("add", ...)` on pristine main `1708faf85b` and on PR head `c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b` with the identical restricted creator (`creatorToolAllowlist: ["read", "cron"]`) creating a trigger-script `systemEvent` job; only the gateway RPC boundary was replaced to capture the params the tool sends.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PROOF_OUT=/tmp/proof-after.txt node_modules/.bin/tsx cron-trigger-proof.ts` (harness invokes the real cron tool `add` with `trigger.script` + `payload.kind=systemEvent`, prints the captured `cron.add` payload)
Evidence after fix:
```

{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed"}
# AFTER (this patch, head c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b, identical input)

```
Observed result after fix: The persisted trigger-script job carries `toolsAllow: ["read","cron"]`, capping the trigger to exactly the creator-visible tools instead of receiving the full coding tool surface.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unsupported OAuth enterprise domain before refresh and model routing
target.body:
## Summary
A legacy `github-copilot` OAuth profile can carry an `enterpriseUrl` that is not a GitHub Copilot host. Current `main` templates that persisted value straight into the endpoint it sends the bearer credential to. The refresh path sends the refresh token to `api.<persisted-domain>`, and the model-routing path derives the completions base URL from the same credential, so an unexpired credential keeps routing its access token to that origin without ever reaching a refresh. No allowlist is applied on either path.

This rejects an off-allowlist persisted origin before a request is issued and before a model URL is produced.

## Root cause
`src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts`. Two egress points, both reachable from persisted state.

Refresh, before:

```ts
export async function refreshGitHubCopilotToken(refreshToken: string, enterpriseDomain?: string) {
  const domain = enterpriseDomain || "github.com";
  const urls = getUrls(domain);
  const raw = await fetchJson(urls.copilotTokenUrl, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${refreshToken}`, ...COPILOT_HEADERS },
  });
```

Model routing, before:

```ts
modifyModels(models: Model[], credentials: OAuthCredentials): Model[] {
  const creds = credentials as CopilotCredentials;
  const domain = creds.enterpriseUrl ? (normalizeDomain(creds.enterpriseUrl) ?? undefined) : undefined;
  const baseUrl = getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(creds.access, domain);
  return models.map((m) => (m.provider === "github-copilot" ? { ...m, baseUrl } : m));
}
```

`normalizeDomain` only parses a hostname, it does not check one. `refreshToken` and `modifyModels` are both live on current `main`: `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts` registers `githubCopilotOAuthProvider` in the built-in OAuth registry, `oauth/index.ts:107` calls `provider.refreshToken(creds)`, and `src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:392-395` calls `oauthProvider.modifyModels(combined, cred)` for every `oauth` credential.

## Fix
An off-allowlist origin means the stored access token may itself have been minted by that origin, so its `proxy-ep` is not trustworthy either. The credential is therefore refused as a whole rather than coerced onto `github.com`, which would present an enterprise-scoped token to the wrong GitHub origin.

```ts
export function getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(token?: string, enterpriseDomain?: string): string {
  if (enterpriseDomain && !isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain(enterpriseDomain)) {
    throw new Error(`Refusing to route GitHub Copilot requests for unsupported enterprise domain "${enterpriseDomain}". ...`);
  }
  ...
}

modifyModels(models: Model[], credentials: OAuthCredentials): Model[] {
  const creds = credentials as CopilotCredentials;
  if (!isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain(creds.enterpriseUrl)) {
    return models.filter((m) => m.provider !== "github-copilot");
  }
  const baseUrl = getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(creds.access, creds.enterpriseUrl);
  return models.map((m) => (m.provider === "github-copilot" ? { ...m, baseUrl } : m));
}
```

`modifyModels` withholds the models rather than throwing, because it runs inside the model-registry loop for every provider and a throw there would break the whole model list. Withholding leaves the access token with no route. `refreshGitHubCopilotToken` rejects before issuing a request, `loginGitHubCopilot` rejects an unsupported host up front, and `formatAuthDoctorHint` points affected users at re-authentication, mirroring the existing qwen-portal hint.

## Why this is the right boundary
Every path that turns a persisted or user-supplied domain into a bearer-bearing URL now validates first: login, refresh, and model routing. Supported hosts are unchanged, `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` data-residency tenants still route and refresh exactly as before, so the compatibility cost falls only on credentials whose origin was never a Copilot host.

Rebased onto current `main`, which moved GitHub Copilot into `extensions/github-copilot`. That plugin owns a `token`-type profile and is a different credential shape; it already resolves its host through the SDK allowlist. The legacy `oauth`-type profile path fixed here is still registered and executable on `main` (the proof below resolves it through the real registry), so this is not obsolete code and the plugin does not already cover it. The allowlist and the new `isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain` predicate move to a dependency-free `plugin-sdk` leaf so the core OAuth runtime can share them without closing a module cycle; `plugin-sdk/provider-auth` re-exports `normalizeGithubCopilotDomain`, so `extensions/github-copilot/domain.ts` keeps its existing import unchanged.

A token's `proxy-ep` is still trusted when the minting origin is on the allowlist, which matches the plugin's own `deriveCopilotApiBaseUrlFromToken`. That trust is exactly what this patch withdraws when the origin is not on the allowlist.

## Rebase notes
Rebased onto `main` at `69554995c1`. Two adjustments were needed to land the same fix against current `main`, neither of which changes the fix:

- `main` (#105888, deadcode export trim) made `getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl` module-private. That un-export is preserved; the guarded function is reached from its file's existing `testing` namespace rather than being re-exported, so the deadcode export baseline stays green.
- The changed-file LOC ratchet forbids growth in production files already over 500 lines, and the guards pushed `github-copilot.ts` from 596 to 617. The six wire and option type declarations were hoisted verbatim into a new `github-copilot.types.ts` leaf, bringing the file to 589. That move is type-only and has zero runtime effect.

## Verification
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles.doctor.test.ts` passes, 31 cases. The 5 new domain and model-routing cases fail on pristine `main` and pass with the patch.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on all 7 changed files.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` reports no error in any changed file (the 3 remaining errors are pre-existing on `main`, in `packages/retry` and `src/media-understanding`).
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` passes on the changed production files.
- Full `pnpm build` not run.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a persisted github-copilot OAuth profile whose `enterpriseUrl` is not a Copilot host sends its bearer refresh token to that origin on refresh, and routes its access token to that origin during model use even when it never refreshes.
Real environment tested: the real built-in OAuth provider registry on pristine main 69554995c1 and on the patched tree at head fa14ac3bd1, resolved through `getOAuthProvider("github-copilot")` exactly as `oauth/index.ts` and `model-registry.ts` do, then driving the real `modifyModels` and `refreshToken` of `githubCopilotOAuthProvider`. The persisted credential, the registry, the provider, the allowlist and the doctor hint are all real; the only thing replaced is the outbound network boundary, a recording `fetch` that captures the URL and Authorization header instead of sending the credential to a real host. Scenarios B and C are unchanged controls.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: resolve `getOAuthProvider("github-copilot")` from the real registry, then for each persisted credential call `provider.modifyModels([gpt-5@github-copilot, claude-sonnet-5@anthropic], credential)` and `await provider.refreshToken(credential)`, recording every outbound request.
Evidence after fix:
```

registry lookup getOAuthProvider("github-copilot") -> GitHub Copilot

A. legacy profile minted by an off-allowlist host
  persisted enterpriseUrl: attacker.example
  model routing:  gpt-5 -> https://api.attacker.example

B. data-residency tenant (control)
  persisted enterpriseUrl: acme.ghe.com
  model routing:  gpt-5 -> https://api.acme.ghe.com
  token refresh:  completed
  requests carrying the credential: 1
    -> https://api.acme.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token   Bearer gho_VICTIM_REFRESH_TOKEN

C. public github.com profile (control)
  persisted enterpriseUrl: (none)
  model routing:  gpt-5 -> https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com
  token refresh:  completed

A. legacy profile minted by an off-allowlist host
  persisted enterpriseUrl: attacker.example
  model routing:  github-copilot withheld, access token has no route
```

target.title: fix(restart): keep deferring when pending inspection fails
target.body:
Fixes #104064.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart deferral treated pending-work inspection exceptions as proof that the gateway was idle. That fail-open path could restart while active work still existed but could not be inspected. The first patch fixed the helper retry behavior, but the config-reload caller still cleared its restartPending guard from onCheckError even though the helper now keeps polling. A later config change could therefore start duplicate deferral loops and competing restart preparation.

## Summary

- Treat pending-count inspection exceptions as unknown pending work instead of safe-to-restart.
- Keep the existing deferral lifecycle active after both initial and later getPendingCount failures.
- Preserve the config-reload restartPending guard when retrying inspection failures.
- Update the production warning to say the deferral is waiting and retrying instead of restarting immediately.
- Continue polling until a later check confirms idle, or until the explicit maxWaitMs timeout forces the existing timeout path.

## Evidence

Exact-head validation on 422023a5d715b3833c1683df674ae6b57662e4a7:

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed; 2 shards, 107 tests.
- node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.non-agents.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-non-agents.tsbuildinfo -> passed.
- ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed.
- ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed.
- pnpm check:loc --base upstream/main --head HEAD -> passed.
- git diff --check -> passed.

Focused behavior covered:

- Initial pending inspection throw calls onCheckError, enters deferral with pending=1, and later emits only after a successful idle check.
- Later polling throw calls onCheckError, keeps polling, and later emits only after a successful idle check.
- Config-reload caller keeps restartPending active after an inspection error; a later config restart request does not create duplicate restart emission work.

## Root Cause

The helper and its production caller disagreed about onCheckError semantics. The helper now treats inspection failure as non-terminal, so the caller must keep its deferral guard active until ready, timeout, cancel, or emission settlement.

## Behavior After This Patch

- Initial inspection throw: calls onCheckError, enters deferral with pending=1, and polls again.
- Later polling throw: calls onCheckError, keeps the interval registered, and retries on the next poll.
- Config reload inspection throw: keeps restartPending true and logs waiting/retrying.
- Confirmed pending=0 still emits restart through the normal ready path.
- Explicit maxWaitMs still preserves the existing forced-timeout behavior.

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's plain-text tool-call repair fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The parser only recognized bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats.

Additionally, three related gaps fixed:

- **Multi-call truncation**: JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, dropping subsequent entries
- **Overly broad stripping**: Without shape validation, ordinary JSON prose was removed from visible text
- **Name-only false positives**: `{"name":"read","status":"ok"}` miscategorized as tool call

Affects Ollama, LM Studio, xAI via `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper`. Observed with Qwen family models.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

**Payload parser** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts`):
- `readJsonToolName`, `hasJsonToolArgs`, `readJsonToolArguments` — multi-field name/args extraction
- `extractJsonToolCallNameAndArgs` returns array — multi-tool wrappers promote all valid entries
- Atomic wrapper rejection: any malformed entry → entire `tool_calls` array rejected
- Non-record argument rejection: arrays/strings/primitives rejected, not coerced
- `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` — scans `{`, validates via `JSON.parse`, requires tool-call shape
- Pre-scan gate: `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` disables JSON stripping when mixed with prose
- Exported `scanJsonObject` and `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` for stream normalizer reuse

**Stream normalizer** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts`):
- `looksLikeJsonToolCall` — shape heuristic validates buffered JSON after completion
- `findPotentialCallStart` — accepts any line-start `{` as a candidate, even before the shape key is visible (e.g. `{"na`). `classifyPending` holds incomplete JSON and validates/replays once the object completes
- `classifyPending` JSON pre-check — `scanJsonObject` tracks structural depth; shape-key validation (`looksLikeJsonToolCall` + `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt`) deferred until the JSON object closes. False positives (non-tool JSON prose) replay as visible text
- Aligned with bracket/XML/Harmony patterns: stream-time withhold + terminal promotion
- `findPotentialCallStart` accepts any line-start `{` as a candidate; `classifyPending` defers shape validation until the JSON object completes — eliminates raw-JSON-plus-tool double-delivery regardless of chunk boundaries

## User Impact

- Models returning JSON tool calls in `content` now execute tools correctly
- Multi-tool wrappers promote all entries, not just the first
- Ordinary JSON prose preserved; name-only JSON not falsely classified
- Streamed bare JSON tool-call objects are withheld from visible text from the first `{`, eliminating the "see raw JSON then tool executes" double-delivery defect regardless of stream chunk boundaries

## Evidence

### Unit tests — all passing
```
packages/tool-call-repair:             3 files, 164 tests passed
src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts:   1 file,  62 tests passed
```

### New regression tests (28 total in payload + stream-normalizer)
Key invariants:
- **Split before shape key** (`{"na` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **Split inside shape key** (`{"name` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **3-way split** before key + mid-object: no leak at any chunk boundary
- **Split before key + terminal done**: promoted to tool call, no raw JSON in text_delta
- Non-tool-call JSON prose (`{"status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Name-only JSON (`{"name":"read","status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Plain JSON object without tool shape yielded as visible text
- `tool_calls` wrapper buffered across multiple chunks
- Non-tool-call JSON replayed as false-positive at done
- Visible prefix before a line-start JSON tool call preserved

### Real behavior proof — DeepSeek API live validation

target.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins
target.body:
Fixes #106189
## Summary

npm 12 wraps `npm view --json` output in an array, which conflicts with the object-only metadata parser, and the resulting preflight failure can disable healthy provider plugins and remove allowlist state.

- Problem: npm 12 array-shaped metadata triggers `"incomplete package metadata"` error and npm view process failures (timeout/network) trigger plugin disablement — both cascade through the update pipeline to disable plugins and remove allowlist/config entries/slots
- Solution: Normalize array-shaped npm output in both parsers, and classify **every pre-install** `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` failure as `metadata-env` so the update loop skips destructive plugin disablement (entry.enabled=false, allowlist removal, slot reset). Package-not-found (E404) remains fail-closed.
- What changed:
  - `src/infra/install-source-utils.ts` — `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` returns `category: "metadata-env"` for all failure paths (timeout, network, invalid JSON, incomplete metadata); E404 still has no category
  - `src/infra/update-check.ts` — `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` unwraps single-element npm 12 arrays
  - `src/plugins/install.ts` — `installPluginFromNpmSpec` propagates `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE` code when category is `"metadata-env"`
  - `src/plugins/update.ts` — `recordFailure` skips `disablePluginConfigEntry` for `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`, preserving entries/allowlist/slots; passes `code` from probe and install results
  - `src/plugins/update.test.ts` — mock adds `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`; metadata-probing test updated to verify state preservation
- What did NOT change: Integrity checks, security-policy failures (SECURITY_SCAN_BLOCKED/FAILED remain fail-closed), multi-version array rejection (rejected, not guessed), product behavior, E404 handling

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #106189
- Related #84256 (partial_overlap: different root cause — recorded-version reuse)
- Related #82368 (partial_overlap: Codex config migration, different root cause)
- Related #102883 (merged PR: fixed sibling install metadata parser npm 12 array handling)

## Motivation

Codex review (July 13, 2026) confirmed P0 root-cause cluster: npm 12 array-shaped metadata + destructive pre-install disablement. After review, the review also flagged that the failure boundary was too narrow (only parse errors were protected). This PR addresses both.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: npm 12 array-shaped metadata preflight + all pre-install `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` failures are now protected from destructive plugin disablement
- Real environment tested: Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64, Node v24.13.1 (npm 11+), branch `fix/npm-env-disable-cascade-106189`, rebased on `7d23570591`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
pnpm test src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts
pnpm test src/plugins/update.test.ts
pnpm test src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts
pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts (19 tests)

$ pnpm test src/plugins/update.test.ts
 ✓ |plugins| src/plugins/update.test.ts (116 tests)

$ pnpm test src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts
 ✓ |cli| src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts (34 tests)

$ pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command.test.ts
 ✓ |cli| src/cli/update-cli/update-command.test.ts (41 tests)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `normalizeNpmViewMetadata` (existing) and `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` (fix B) both accept single-element arrays from npm 12
  2. `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` marks **every** failure path with `category: "metadata-env"` — process exits (timeout, network), invalid JSON, incomplete metadata — EXCEPT E404 (package-not-found remains fail-closed)
  3. `installPluginFromNpmSpec` propagates `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE` code when category is `"metadata-env"`
  4. `recordFailure` in the update loop skips `disablePluginConfigEntry` when code is `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`, keeping plugin entries, allowlist, deny, slots, and install records unchanged
  5. Real plugin/integrity/security failures remain fail-closed — only the pre-install metadata resolution is affected

- What was not tested: Live npm 12 end-to-end; macOS/Windows; non-npm registries; network-level fault injection

## Root Cause

| Problem | Introduced | Author | Intent |
|---------|-----------|--------|--------|
| `normalizeNpmViewMetadata` object-only parser | `0946e37523` (Apr 23) | steipete | Designed for npm 11 single-object output — **fixed by `96f0983a85` (Jul 11, PR #102883)** |
| `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` rejects arrays | `62fad3da86` (Jun 17) | Vincent Koc | Same-era design, missed npm 12 fix — **fixed here** |
| `disableOnFailure` with no failure classification | `7c0f5463a5` (May 4) | Vincent Koc | Isolate broken plugin packages — **fixed here** |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw plugins update --all` no longer disable healthy plugins when npm view metadata fails for any reason (format incompatibility, timeout, network error)
- `openclaw doctor --fix` or `openclaw update repair` can recover plugins disabled by earlier npm 12 failures

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

- What you did NOT verify: Live npm 12 environment; macOS/Windows runtime; network-level fault injection

- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — full pre-install failure boundary (47 lines), preserves integrity/security fail-closed, E404 remains fail-closed
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Pinning npm version (workaround); removing multi-version rejection (weakens integrity); broad `disableOnFailure` removal (hides real plugin failures); parse-error-only boundary (rejected by Codex review — too narrow)

## AI Assistance

- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema` receives a null or non-object schema (e.g., from `codex_app__automation_update` tool with no user automations configured), it was returning `schema: null` which causes strict providers like DeepSeek to reject the entire tool list with HTTP 400.

Error from DeepSeek:
```
Invalid schema for function 'codex_app__automation_update': schema must be a JSON Schema of 'type: "object"', got 'type: null'
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-schema-json-projection.ts:162-163`. When the schema is not a JSON object (e.g., null, primitive, array), the function adds a violation but still returns `schema: null`. Strict providers like DeepSeek validate function schemas and reject any schema that is not of `type: "object"\.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Users with DeepSeek provider would get HTTP 400 errors when the Codex endpoint tries to send tools with null schemas (e.g., no user automations configured).
- **After**: Tools with null schemas are projected to a default empty object schema `{ type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false }`, allowing the request to proceed while still reporting the violation for debugging.

## Evidence

### Root Cause Analysis

1. Issue #106277 reports: `codex_app__automation_update` tool has `type: null` schema
2. The tool is defined in Codex extension with no user automations configured, so `tool.parameters` is `null`
3. `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema(null, ...)` returns `{ schema: null, violations: [...] }`
4. DeepSeek rejects the entire tool list because `null` is not a valid JSON Schema object

The fix returns a default empty object schema when the input is not a JSON object:

```typescript
if (!isJsonObject(projection.schema)) {
  violations.push(`${path} must be a JSON object schema`);
  // Return a default empty object schema when the input is not a JSON object
  return {
    schema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: {},
      required: [],
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
    violations,
  };
}
```

target.title: fix(discord): preserve tool updates when progress preview is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #87704. In Discord `streaming.mode=progress`, OpenClaw could suppress standalone tool/block progress messages even when the progress preview lane never produced a visible draft. That left operators without visible tool updates during default progress-mode fast-tool turns.

A follow-up gap remained when an empty progress preview later produced a final response: the deferred progress block could be dropped before the final message, so users still missed the only visible tool update for that turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Expose default tool-progress suppression only after the progress compositor has actually started a visible progress draft in `progress` mode.
- Keep immediate suppression for configurations that can render a label-only progress draft, so existing visible-preview behavior is preserved.
- Defer Discord text-only block replies that may be replaced by a progress draft; if the draft stays empty, flush the deferred block before the final reply.
- Drop deferred interim blocks once a progress draft becomes visible, preventing the existing duplicate `on it` plus draft behavior.

## User Impact
Discord operators keep seeing meaningful fast-tool/block updates when progress preview mode is enabled but has no visible content yet. If a final reply arrives after an empty preview lane, the deferred progress block is delivered before that final message instead of being lost.

Existing visible progress drafts still own the progress lane, so users do not get duplicated interim block messages after real progress appears.

## Evidence
Head commit: `f2aa368ec554a0ce2dedfa2357f9fd3b85a9b56e`.

Real behavior proof from the Discord and channel compositor harnesses:

- Default Discord progress mode with no visible draft: `replyOptions.suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages` is `undefined`, `draftStream.update` is not called, and one fallback block reply is delivered with text `fast command finished`.
- Empty Discord progress preview followed by a final reply: the deferred block is flushed before the final reply so both the tool update and final answer are visible in order.
- Discord progress mode after work expands: the draft updates to `Shelling` with the exec progress lines, the earlier text-only interim block is not delivered, and the final reply edits the preview to `done`.
- Channel compositor: `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages` is `false` before the progress draft starts, stays `false` after the first delayed work event, and becomes `true` after the second work event starts the visible draft.

Validation:

target.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unsupported OAuth enterprise domain before refresh and model routing
target.body:
## Summary
A legacy `github-copilot` OAuth profile can carry an `enterpriseUrl` that is not a GitHub Copilot host. Current `main` templates that persisted value straight into the endpoint it sends the bearer credential to. The refresh path sends the refresh token to `api.<persisted-domain>`, and the model-routing path derives the completions base URL from the same credential, so an unexpired credential keeps routing its access token to that origin without ever reaching a refresh. No allowlist is applied on either path.

This rejects an off-allowlist persisted origin before a request is issued and before a model URL is produced.

## Root cause
`src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts`. Two egress points, both reachable from persisted state.

Refresh, before:

```ts
export async function refreshGitHubCopilotToken(refreshToken: string, enterpriseDomain?: string) {
  const domain = enterpriseDomain || "github.com";
  const urls = getUrls(domain);
  const raw = await fetchJson(urls.copilotTokenUrl, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${refreshToken}`, ...COPILOT_HEADERS },
  });
```

Model routing, before:

```ts
modifyModels(models: Model[], credentials: OAuthCredentials): Model[] {
  const creds = credentials as CopilotCredentials;
  const domain = creds.enterpriseUrl ? (normalizeDomain(creds.enterpriseUrl) ?? undefined) : undefined;
  const baseUrl = getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(creds.access, domain);
  return models.map((m) => (m.provider === "github-copilot" ? { ...m, baseUrl } : m));
}
```

`normalizeDomain` only parses a hostname, it does not check one. `refreshToken` and `modifyModels` are both live on current `main`: `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts` registers `githubCopilotOAuthProvider` in the built-in OAuth registry, `oauth/index.ts:107` calls `provider.refreshToken(creds)`, and `src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:392-395` calls `oauthProvider.modifyModels(combined, cred)` for every `oauth` credential.

## Fix
An off-allowlist origin means the stored access token may itself have been minted by that origin, so its `proxy-ep` is not trustworthy either. The credential is therefore refused as a whole rather than coerced onto `github.com`, which would present an enterprise-scoped token to the wrong GitHub origin.

```ts
export function getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(token?: string, enterpriseDomain?: string): string {
  if (enterpriseDomain && !isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain(enterpriseDomain)) {
    throw new Error(`Refusing to route GitHub Copilot requests for unsupported enterprise domain "${enterpriseDomain}". ...`);
  }
  ...
}

modifyModels(models: Model[], credentials: OAuthCredentials): Model[] {
  const creds = credentials as CopilotCredentials;
  if (!isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain(creds.enterpriseUrl)) {
    return models.filter((m) => m.provider !== "github-copilot");
  }
  const baseUrl = getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(creds.access, creds.enterpriseUrl);
  return models.map((m) => (m.provider === "github-copilot" ? { ...m, baseUrl } : m));
}
```

`modifyModels` withholds the models rather than throwing, because it runs inside the model-registry loop for every provider and a throw there would break the whole model list. Withholding leaves the access token with no route. `refreshGitHubCopilotToken` rejects before issuing a request, `loginGitHubCopilot` rejects an unsupported host up front, and `formatAuthDoctorHint` points affected users at re-authentication, mirroring the existing qwen-portal hint.

## Why this is the right boundary
Every path that turns a persisted or user-supplied domain into a bearer-bearing URL now validates first: login, refresh, and model routing. Supported hosts are unchanged, `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` data-residency tenants still route and refresh exactly as before, so the compatibility cost falls only on credentials whose origin was never a Copilot host.

Rebased onto current `main`, which moved GitHub Copilot into `extensions/github-copilot`. That plugin owns a `token`-type profile and is a different credential shape; it already resolves its host through the SDK allowlist. The legacy `oauth`-type profile path fixed here is still registered and executable on `main` (the proof below resolves it through the real registry), so this is not obsolete code and the plugin does not already cover it. The allowlist and the new `isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain` predicate move to a dependency-free `plugin-sdk` leaf so the core OAuth runtime can share them without closing a module cycle; `plugin-sdk/provider-auth` re-exports `normalizeGithubCopilotDomain`, so `extensions/github-copilot/domain.ts` keeps its existing import unchanged.

A token's `proxy-ep` is still trusted when the minting origin is on the allowlist, which matches the plugin's own `deriveCopilotApiBaseUrlFromToken`. That trust is exactly what this patch withdraws when the origin is not on the allowlist.

## Rebase notes
Rebased onto `main` at `69554995c1`. Two adjustments were needed to land the same fix against current `main`, neither of which changes the fix:

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
